dervis-irab:1-6.t:
* I'rab:
(سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ): «سبّح» is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; «لله» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سبّح». It was also said that the lām is redundant (zāʾida) with the object. The discussion of this verb has preceded, and that it is sometimes transitive by itself and at other times with the lām. This verb came in some of the openings (of surahs) as a past verb, as in this opening, in some as an imperfect, and in some as an imperative, to indicate that these things glorify (Allah) at all times. «ما» is the fāʿil (agent) of «سبّح»; «في السموات» is attached to an omitted element that is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; «الأرض» is conjoined to «السموات». The wāw is circumstantial or resumptive; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «العزيز» a first khabar (predicate) and «الحكيم» a second khabar. He expressed it with «ما» rather than «من» by giving precedence to the majority (taghlīb).
(لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ): «له» is a fronted khabar and «ملك السموات» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «الأرض» is conjoined to «السموات». The clause «يحيي» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «له», or resumptive. The clause «له ملك السموات» is resumptive and has no grammatical position.
(وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «قدير» its khabar; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «قدير».
(هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْباطِنُ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ): «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «الأول» its khabar, and what follows is conjoined to it; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «عليم» its khabar; «بكل شيء» is attached to «عليم».
(هُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَوى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ): «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «الذي» its khabar; the clause «خلق السموات والأرض» is the ṣila of the relative noun and has no grammatical position; «في ستة أيام» is attached to «خلق»; «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence with delay; «استوى» is a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), referring to Allah; «على العرش» is attached to «استوى».
(يَعْلَمُ ما يَلِجُ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَما يَخْرُجُ مِنْها): the clause «يعلم» is circumstantial or resumptive; «يعلم» is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "هو"; «في الأرض» is attached to «يلج»; «ما يخرج منها» is conjoined to «ما يلج في الأرض»; «منها» is attached to «يخرج».
(وَما يَنْزِلُ مِنَ السَّماءِ وَما يَعْرُجُ فِيها): «وما» is conjoined to the first «ما», and «ما يعرج فيها» is also conjoined.
(وَهُوَ مَعَكُمْ أَيْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ; «معكم» is an adverb of place attached to an omitted khabar. «أينما» is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, and it is attached to its omitted answer. «كنتم» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then He is with you"; and «كنتم» is complete (tāmma) [Translator's note: the source calls «كنتم» both defective (nāqiṣ) and complete (tāmma) here; translated as written]. «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and «بصير» the khabar; «بما تعملون» is attached to «بصير»; the clause «تعملون» is the ṣila of the relative noun and has no grammatical position.
(لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ): «له» is a fronted khabar and «ملك السموات» is its khabar [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably "its mubtadaʾ" is meant]; «إلى الله» is attached to «ترجع»; «ترجع» is a passive imperfect verb and «الأمور» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
(يُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهارِ وَيُولِجُ النَّهارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ): the clause is circumstantial or resumptive; «الليل» is the object of «يولج»; «في النهار» is attached to «يولج», and what follows is conjoined to it.
(وَهُوَ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ): the wāw is a conjunction; «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «عليم» its khabar; «بذات الصدور» is attached to «عليم».

dervis-irab:7-10.t:
* I'rab:
(آمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَأَنْفِقُوا مِمَّا جَعَلَكُمْ مُسْتَخْلَفِينَ فِيهِ): resumptive speech, set forth to begin addressing the unbelievers of Quraysh and commanding them to believe, after He had mentioned kinds of proofs of the divine oneness. «آمنوا» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); «بالله» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «آمنوا»; «رسوله» is conjoined to it; «أنفقوا» is conjoined to «آمنوا»; «مما» is attached to «أنفقوا»; the clause «جعلكم» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the kāf is the first object and «مستخلفين» the second object of «جعل»; «فيه» is attached to «مستخلفين», i.e. of acquired wealth and gathered equipment.
(فَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْكُمْ وَأَنْفَقُوا لَهُمْ أَجْرٌ كَبِيرٌ): the fāʾ is resumptive; «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; «منكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «أنفقوا» is conjoined to «آمنوا», falling within the scope of the ṣila; «لهم» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «أجر» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «كبير» is a naʿt (adjective); the clause «لهم أجر كبير» is the khabar of «الذين».
(وَما لَكُمْ لا تُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ): the wāw is resumptive; «ما» is a noun of disapproving interrogation, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; «لكم» is the khabar; the clause «لا تؤمنون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl; «بالله» is attached to «تؤمنون». The meaning is: what thing has become settled for you while you are not believing? The wāw is circumstantial; «الرسول» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «يدعوكم» is the khabar; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the wāw in «تؤمنون».
(لِتُؤْمِنُوا بِرَبِّكُمْ وَقَدْ أَخَذَ مِيثاقَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ): the lām is for causation; «تؤمنوا» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يدعوكم»; «بربكم» is attached to «تؤمنوا». The wāw is circumstantial; «قد» is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); «أخذ ميثاقكم» is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of «يدعوكم», also by way of overlapping (tadākhul) [i.e. a ḥāl within a ḥāl]. In one reading it is «أُخِذ» in the passive, so «ميثاقكم» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); i.e. His setting up proofs for you and enabling you to reflect is equivalent to taking the covenant. It was also said that it is a reference to His making them testify about themselves in His saying «ألست بربكم قالوا بلى». «إن» is conditional; «كنتم» is a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: "then now the signs of certainty have appeared, the proofs and demonstrations have become clear, and the rational and transmitted arguments have become binding on you"; «مؤمنين» is the khabar of «كنتم».
(هُوَ الَّذِي يُنَزِّلُ عَلى عَبْدِهِ آياتٍ بَيِّناتٍ لِيُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إِلَى النُّورِ): «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «الذي» its khabar; the clause «ينزل» is the ṣila and has no grammatical position; «على عبده» is attached to «ينزل»; «آيات» is a mafʿūl bihi and «بيّنات» an adjective. The lām is for causation; «يخرجكم» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «ينزل»; «من الظلمات» is attached to «يخرجكم», i.e. from unbelief; «إلى النور» is also attached to «يخرجكم», i.e. to faith.
(وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُمْ لَرَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; «إنّ» and its noun; «بكم» is attached to «رءوف»; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); «رءوف» is the first khabar of «إنّ» and «رحيم» the second khabar of «إنّ».
(وَما لَكُمْ أَلَّا تُنْفِقُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَلِلَّهِ مِيراثُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ): the wāw is resumptive; «ما» is a noun of disapproving interrogation, a mubtadaʾ; «لكم» is the khabar; «أن» is a maṣdar-forming particle that makes the verb accusative; «لا» is negating; «تنفقوا» is an imperfect verb made accusative by «أن»; «أن» with what follows it is interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) in the position of accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "in not spending" or "from not spending", and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl. «في سبيل الله» is attached to «تنفقوا». The wāw is circumstantial; «لله» is a fronted khabar and «ميراث السموات» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «الأرض» is conjoined to «السموات»; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of the settling (istiqrār) or of its object; i.e. and what thing prevents you from spending in the way of Allah, while the inheritance of the heavens and the earth belongs to Him?
(لا يَسْتَوِي مِنْكُمْ مَنْ أَنْفَقَ مِنْ قَبْلِ الْفَتْحِ وَقاتَلَ): resumptive speech, set forth to explain the difference in the ranks of those who spend. «لا» is negating; «يستوي» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); «منكم» is a ḥāl; «من» is its fāʿil; the clause «أنفق» is the ṣila of the relative noun and has no grammatical position; «من قبل الفتح» is attached to «أنفق»; «قاتل» is conjoined to «أنفق». There is an omission in the speech that will be mentioned in the Rhetoric section.
(أُولئِكَ أَعْظَمُ دَرَجَةً مِنَ الَّذِينَ أَنْفَقُوا مِنْ بَعْدُ وَقاتَلُوا): «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to those who spent; «أعظم» is the khabar; «درجة» is a tamyīz (specification); «من الذين» is attached to «أعظم»; the clause «أنفقوا» is the ṣila; «من بعد» is attached to «أنفقوا»; «قاتلوا» is conjoined to «أنفقوا».
(وَكُلًّا وَعَدَ اللَّهُ الْحُسْنى): «الله» is the fāʿil of «وعد» and «الحسنى» is the second mafʿūl bihi; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and «خبير» its khabar, and «بما تعملون» is attached to «خبير». [Translator's note: the source does not parse «كلا» (the first object) here, and the last part refers to the end of the verse, «والله بما تعملون خبير», which is not quoted.]

* Rhetoric:
1- Omission (al-ḥadhf): omission in these verses is frequent, and we summarise it as follows:
- The object of «أنفقوا» is omitted for intensity in urging spending and not being stingy with wealth.
- The object of «تنفقوا في سبيل الله» is omitted for the reason already given, and to intensify the rebuke, i.e. and what is with you that you do not spend what is a means of drawing near to Allah the Exalted?
- The second of the two things being equal is omitted, because equality (istiwāʾ) is only complete with two things, so a muḍāf must be omitted, its implied form being: "Not equal among you are the one who spent before the conquest of Mecca and the strength of Islam and the one who spent after the conquest"; it was omitted because the indication of it is clear. Abū Ḥayyān's words on this point: "What is apparent is that «من» is the fāʿil of «لا يستوي», and its counterpart, namely «ومن أنفق من بعد الفتح وقاتل», is omitted because the meaning is clear. «أولئك», i.e. those who spent before the conquest, before Islam spread and became widespread and before the Muslims took control of the Mother of Towns (Mecca); they are the first forerunners among the Emigrants (Muhājirūn) and the Helpers (Anṣār), about whom the saying of the Prophet ﷺ came: 'If one of you were to spend the like of Uḥud in gold, he would not reach the mudd of one of them, nor half of it.' Far-fetched is the one who held that the fāʿil of «لا يستوي» is a pronoun referring to spending, i.e. it — spending, i.e. its genus — is not equal, since some of it is before the conquest and some after; and that «من أنفق» is a mubtadaʾ, and «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is what follows it, the clause being in the position of nominative as the khabar of «من». This involves breaking up the speech and departing from the apparent sense without necessity. Omitting the conjoined element because the counterpart indicates it is frequent." Spending and fighting before the conquest were better than spending and fighting after the conquest only because the people's need was greater at that time, and they were fewer and weaker.
2- In His saying «في سبيل الله» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), i.e. obedience to Him; and the way of Allah is every good that leads them to Him.

dervis-irab:11-15.t:
* Vocabulary:
(انْظُرُونا): an imperative from naẓar (looking). Naẓar is turning the eye toward the direction in which the visible thing whose seeing is intended lies. Among what indicates this is the poet's saying:
فيا ميّ هل يجزى بكائي بمثله ... مرارا وأنفاسي إليك الزوافر
وإني متى أشرف على الجانب الذي ... به أنت من بين الجوانب ناظر
(O Mayy, will my weeping be repaid with its like, time and again, and my sighs that rise toward you? Whenever I come upon the side, among all sides, where you are, I am looking.)
For if naẓar were seeing (ruʾya), he would not ask for repayment for it, because the lover does not seek any reward for looking at his beloved; rather he wants that and longs for it. Also indicating this is the other poet's saying:
ونظرة ذي شجن وامق ... إذا ما الركائب جاوزن ميلا
(And the look of a grieving, loving man when the riding camels have passed a mile.)
As for His saying, glorified is He, «ولا ينظر إليهم يوم القيامة», the meaning is that He, glorified is He, does not grant them His mercy. You may say "So-and-so looked at me" when he grants you something, and a speaker says "Look at me, may Allah look at you", meaning "grant me good, may Allah grant you". The verb naẓartu and what is inflected from it is used in several ways:
1- The first is that you mean by it "I looked at the thing", omitting the preposition and making the verb reach the object directly. Among this is what Abū al-Ḥasan recited:
ظاهرات الجمال والحسن ينظر ... ن كما ينظر الأراك الظباء
(Of manifest beauty and loveliness, they look as the gazelles look at the arāk trees.)
The meaning is "they look at the arāk", and the preposition was omitted. For this reason Abū Ḥayyān said: "Naẓar in the sense of seeing is not transitive by itself except in poetry; it is only transitive with «إلى»."
2- The second is that you mean by it "I contemplated and considered"; it is an intransitive verb. Among this is their saying "Go and look at Zayd, whose father is he?"; by this contemplation is meant. Among this is His saying «انظر كيف ضربوا لك الأمثال» and «انظر كيف فضلنا بعضهم على بعض». This may be made transitive with a preposition, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted «أفلا ينظرون إلى الإبل كيف خلقت», which is an urging to contemplate; and it may be made transitive with «في», as in His saying «أفلم ينظروا في ملكوت السموات والأرض». As for the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
فلما بدا حوران والآل دونه ... نظرت فلم تنظر بعينك منظرا
(When Ḥawrān appeared with the mirage before it, you looked, but your eye looked on no sight.)
it may be "you looked, but you did not see with your eye a sight" toward the āl, i.e. the mirage. It has also been allowed that by naẓar he meant seeing in an extended sense, because turning the sight toward the thing seen is followed by seeing, and a thing may be called by the word for what follows it and is joined to it, as in their calling the water-skin rāwiya [Translator's note: rāwiya is originally the camel that carries the water]. And "you looked but did not look" may be like "you spoke but did not speak", i.e. you did not produce speech as it was wanted; likewise "you looked but your eye did not look on a sight" as you wanted, or did not see a sight that pleases.
3- The third is that you mean by it "I waited for him". Among this is His saying «غير ناظرين إناه», and like it the saying of al-Farazdaq:
نظرت كما انتظرت الله حتى ... كفاك الماحلين لك المحالا
(I waited as you waited for Allah, until He sufficed you against those who plotted guile against you.)
He means "I waited as you waited."
4- The fourth is that anẓartu is in the sense of intaẓartu (I waited), where by your saying "anẓirnī" you seek the respite that waiting requires. Among this is the saying of ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm:
أبا هند فلا تعجل علينا ... وأنظرنا نخبرك اليقينا
(O Abū Hind, do not be hasty against us; give us respite and we will tell you the certain truth.)
And among this is His saying «فأنظرني إلى يوم يبعثون»; it is only a request for respite and postponement. On this basis is the reading of Ḥamza «أَنظِرونا» with the hamza of disjunction (qaṭʿ) and the ẓāʾ with kasra.
(يُقْرِضُ): qarḍ (loan) is what you give someone else so that he repays it to you; it is cutting it off from its owner with his permission on the guarantee of returning its like. The Arabs say: "I have with you a loan of truth" and "a loan of evil" when someone has done him good or evil. The poet said:
ويقضي سلامان بن مفرج قرضها ... بما قدّمت أيديهم وأزلت
(And Salāmān ibn Mufarrij will repay its loan for what their hands sent forth and conferred.)
More on its meaning here will come in the Rhetoric section.

* I'rab:
(مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً فَيُضاعِفَهُ لَهُ وَلَهُ أَجْرٌ كَرِيمٌ): there are several views on it. One of them is that «من» is interrogative, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), «ذا» is a demonstrative that is its khabar (predicate), and «الذي» is an adjective of it or a badal (substitute) for it. It is valid for «من ذا» to be an interrogative on its own, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, with «الذي» as its khabar. It is also valid for «ذا» to be the mubtadaʾ, «الذي يقرض الله» an adjective, and «من» the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, placed before it because of the meaning of interrogation in it. «يقرض» is an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; «الله» is its object; «قرضا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and «حسنا» a naʿt (adjective). The fāʾ is causal (sababiyya); «يضاعفه» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the fāʾ, as an answer to the interrogative. It was also read in the nominative, as resumption or conjunction. Abū Ḥayyān has a fine discussion here which we quote as follows: "ʿĀṣim read «فيضاعفَه» in the accusative with the fāʿ as an answer to the interrogative. There is unease in this, said Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī, because the question did not fall on the lending; the question only fell on the doer of the lending, and the fāʾ only makes accusative a verb referred back to a verb being asked about. But this group — meaning of the readers — took it according to the sense, as though His saying «من ذا الذي يقرض» were equivalent to His saying 'Will anyone lend to Allah so that He multiplies it?' This view that Abū ʿAlī held — that the fāʾ only makes accusative a verb referred back to a verb being asked about — is not correct. Rather it is permissible when the interrogation is by its nominal particles, as in 'Who calls me, so that I answer him?', 'Where is your house, so that I visit you?', 'When do you travel, so that I accompany you?' and 'How will you be, so that I keep you company?'. The interrogation here concerns the person of the caller, the adverb of place, the adverb of time and the state, not the verb. Ibn Kaysān reported from the Arabs: 'Where did Zayd go, so that we follow him?', likewise 'How much is your wealth, so that we may spend it?' and 'Who is your father, so that we honour him?', with the accusative after the fāʾ. The reading «فيضاعفه» in the accusative is a mutawātir reading, and the verb occurs as the ṣila of «الذي», «الذي» is an adjective of «ذا», and «ذا» is its khabar [i.e. of «من»]. If the accusative is permissible in a case like this, its permissibility in the preceding examples is all the more fitting." «له» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يضاعفه». The wāw is circumstantial; «له» is a fronted khabar and «أجر» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «كريم» is an adjective.
(يَوْمَ تَرَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ يَسْعى نُورُهُمْ بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَبِأَيْمانِهِمْ): «يوم» is an adverb attached to the settling (istiqrār) that governs «وله أجر», i.e. a reward is settled for him on that day; or to an implied verb, its implied form being "they will be rewarded"; [or] made accusative by "remember", so that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Abū al-Baqāʾ said: its governor is «فيضاعفه». The clause «ترى المؤمنين والمؤمنات» is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it. The clause «يسعى نورهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), because the seeing is visual; «نورهم» is the fāʿil of «يسعى»; the adverb is attached to «يسعى»; «بأيمانهم» is conjoined to «أيديهم».
(بُشْراكُمُ الْيَوْمَ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ خالِدِينَ فِيها ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْعَظِيمُ): the clause is the speech quoted by an omitted verb of saying, i.e. "and it will be said to them". «بشراكم» is a mubtadaʾ; «اليوم» is an adverb attached to the omitted saying; «جنات» is the khabar of «بشراكم»; the clause «تجري من تحتها الأنهار» is an adjective of «جنات»; «خالدين» is a ḥāl, and its governor is the omitted muḍāf, since the implied form is "your good tidings are your entering gardens, abiding in them"; the fāʿil, namely the pronoun of the addressees, was omitted and the maṣdar (verbal noun) was annexed to its object, so it became "entering gardens"; then the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi was put in its place in the i'rab. «فيها» is attached to «خالدين». «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ, «هو» a second mubtadaʾ and «الفوز» its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «ذلك»; «العظيم» is an adjective of «الفوز».
(يَوْمَ يَقُولُ الْمُنافِقُونَ وَالْمُنافِقاتُ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا انْظُرُونا نَقْتَبِسْ مِنْ نُورِكُمْ): the adverb is a badal for the «يوم» before it. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "It appears to me that its governor is «ذلك هو الفوز العظيم», as if He were saying that the believers win mercy on the day when such-and-such befalls the hypocrites, because a man's triumph on the day his enemy is extinguished is more marvellous and more splendid." Abū Ḥayyān rejected this. The clause «يقول المنافقون» is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; «المنافقات» is conjoined to «المنافقون»; «للذين» is attached to «يقول»; the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila; the clause «انظرونا» is the speech quoted (maqūl al-qawl). This is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; «نا» is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi. «نقتبس» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the request, i.e. we will take light; «من نوركم» is attached to «نقتبس».
(قِيلَ ارْجِعُوا وَراءَكُمْ فَالْتَمِسُوا نُوراً): «قيل» is a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, referring to the believers or to the angels charged with them [Translator's note: so in the source]. «ارجعوا» is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the speech quoted. «وراءكم» is an adverb attached to «ارجعوا», i.e. go back to the place of standing, to where we were given this light, and seek another light, since you have no way to this light. Abū al-Baqāʾ chose that «وراءكم» be a verbal noun of command (ism fiʿl amr) containing a pronoun as fāʿil, i.e. "go back, go back", and he refused that it be an adverb of «ارجعوا», saying: because of its little benefit, since going back is only ever to the rear. This is not sound. The fāʾ is a conjunction; «التمسوا» is an imperative verb conjoined to «ارجعوا»; «نورا» is a mafʿūl bihi.
(فَضُرِبَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِسُورٍ لَهُ بابٌ باطِنُهُ فِيهِ الرَّحْمَةُ وَظاهِرُهُ مِنْ قِبَلِهِ الْعَذابُ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; «ضرب» is a passive past verb; «بسور» is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil. It was also said that the adverb is the nāʾib fāʿil, and it was said that the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) with the nāʾib fāʿil, i.e. a wall was set up between them. The clause is conjoined to His saying «قيل ارجعوا», for when the believers or the angels prevented them from catching up with them to take from their light, those hypocrites remained in a dense darkness in which the eye does not glimpse any spark from its side. More of this meaning will come in the Rhetoric section. «له» is a fronted khabar and «باب» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is an adjective of «سور». «باطنه» is a mubtadaʾ; «فيه» is a fronted khabar and «الرحمة» a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause «فيه [الرحمة]» is the khabar of «باطنه», and the clause is a second adjective of «سور», or an adjective of «باب»; perhaps this is preferable because of its nearness, since the pronoun refers to the nearest unless there is a contextual indication, and none is determined here. «وظاهره»: the wāw is a conjunction; «ظاهره» is a mubtadaʾ; «من قبله» is a fronted khabar and «العذاب» a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause is the khabar of «ظاهره», and the whole clause is conjoined to the one before it.
(يُنادُونَهُمْ: أَلَمْ نَكُنْ مَعَكُمْ): the clause «ينادونهم» is resumptive; it was also said that it is a ḥāl of the pronoun in the adverb. The hamza is an interrogative particle; «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) [i.e. turning the imperfect into past meaning] and jussive; «نكن» is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb whose noun is latent, its implied form being "نحن"; «معكم» is an adverb attached to an omitted khabar. The interrogative clause is explicative and has no grammatical position, or it is in the accusative by an implied verb of saying.
(قالُوا بَلى وَلكِنَّكُمْ فَتَنْتُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ وَتَرَبَّصْتُمْ وَارْتَبْتُمْ): «قالوا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «بلى» is a particle of answer; «لكنكم» is «لكنّ» and its noun; the clause «فتنتم أنفسكم» is the khabar of «لكنكم»; «تربصتم» and «ارتبتم» are conjoined to «فتنتم». The complements of the three verbs are omitted, i.e. you tempted yourselves with hypocrisy, you awaited misfortunes for the believers, and you doubted about the religion.
(وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الْأَمانِيُّ حَتَّى جاءَ أَمْرُ اللَّهِ وَغَرَّكُمْ بِاللَّهِ الْغَرُورُ): the wāw is a conjunction, [followed by] a verb and its fāʿil; «حتى» is a particle of limit and of the genitive; «جاء أمر الله» is a verb and its fāʿil, i.e. death; «غرّكم» is conjoined to «وغرتكم»; «بالله» is attached to «غرّكم»; «الغرور» is the fāʿil, i.e. Satan.
(فَالْيَوْمَ لا يُؤْخَذُ مِنْكُمْ فِدْيَةٌ وَلا مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا): the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition), i.e. if you wish to know your end and your destinies, then today... «اليوم» is an adverb attached to «يؤخذ»; «لا» is negating; «يؤخذ» is a passive imperfect verb; «منكم» is also attached to «يؤخذ»; «فدية» is the nāʾib fāʿil. The verb is masculine because the femininity is figurative; it was also read «تؤخذ» with the tāʾ. «ولا من الذين كفروا» is conjoined to «منكم», and the clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun.
(مَأْواكُمُ النَّارُ هِيَ مَوْلاكُمْ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ): «مأواكم النار» is a fronted khabar and a postponed mubtadaʾ, or the reverse; «هي» is a mubtadaʾ and «مولاكم» the khabar. «مولاكم» may validly be in the sense of "more fitting for you". Labīd said:
فغدت كلا الفرجين تحسب أنه ... مولى المخافة خلفها وأمامها
(So she went off at dawn, thinking each of the two openings to be the proper place of fear, behind her and before her.)
It is from his Muʿallaqa, describing a wild cow. The farj is the place of fear, and what is between the legs of animals: what is between the forelegs is a farj and what is between the hind legs is a farj. Thaʿlab said that mawlā in this verse means "the more fitting for the thing", like the saying of Allah the Exalted «مأواكم النار هي مولاكم», i.e. more fitting for you. He says: that cow went off at dawn thinking that each of her two openings was the mawlā of fear, i.e. its place and its owner; or thinking that each of her two openings was the more fitting for fear, i.e. for being feared. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: by "the fear" he meant the dogs, and by its mawlā their owner; i.e. she went off not knowing whether the dogs and the dog-master [Translator's note: the source has «الكلاب والكلاب»; it may mean "the dogs and the dog-handler (kallāb)" or be a duplication] were behind her or in front of her, so she supposed each of the two directions to be a place of the dogs. The pronoun that is the noun of «أنّ» refers to «كلا», which is singular in form even though it contains the meaning of the dual; what comes after it may be construed once according to its form and another time according to its meaning, and construing according to the form is more frequent. Their illustration is: "كلا أخويك سبّني" (both your brothers insulted me — singular verb) and "كلا أخويك سبّاني" (dual verb). The poet said:
كلاهما حين جدّ الجري بينهما ... قد أقلعا وكلا أنفيهما رابي
(Both of them, when the race between them grew earnest, stopped, and each of their two noses was swelling with breath.)
He construed «أقلعا» according to the meaning of «كلا» and «رابيا» according to its form. And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said «كلتا الجنتين آتت أكلها» [Translator's note: the source quotes it as «كلتا الجنتين قد آتت أكلها»; the Quranic text has no «قد»], construing according to the form of «كلتا». «خلفها وأمامها» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "it is behind her and before her"; it may also be a badal for «كلا الفرجين», its implied form being "So she went off, each of the two openings, behind her and before her, she thinking it to be the place of fear". The real meaning of «مولاكم» is "your fitting place (maḥrākum, maqmanukum)"; one says "he is ḥarī to do such-and-such" and "he is qamīn to do it", i.e. worthy of that and deserving of it; i.e. your place of which it is said "it is more fitting for you", as it was said "he is a maʾinna of generosity", i.e. a place for a speaker's saying "indeed he is generous". So it is a noun of place, but not like other nouns of place, for those are a place of the event regardless of who it issues from; this is a likeness of the one preferred over another, which is its attribute, so the meaning of "more fitting (awlā)" is regarded in it because it is derived from it, just as maʾinna is taken from «إنّ» without being derived from it. It may also be meant that it is your helper, i.e. you have no helper but the Fire. «بئس» is a non-inflecting (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; «المصير» is the fāʿil; and the one specified for blame is omitted, i.e. the Fire.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا» there is a dependent explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tabaʿiyya): He likened spending in the way of Allah to lending to Him, then omitted the thing likened and kept the thing it is likened to; what unites them is giving something for a return. The meaning of its being "goodly" is that it is free from the taints of showing off. As for the loan given to a person of wealth on condition that its equivalent be returned, it is an emphasised sunna; it may be obligatory for one in dire need, and forbidden to one who uses it to help himself to disobedience.
2- In His saying «يسعى نورهم بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم» there is a primary explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya aṣliyya): the light is a metaphor for the guidance and the good pleasure in which they are; the thing likened was omitted and the thing it is likened to was kept.
3- In His saying «خالدين فيها» after His saying «بشراكم اليوم» there is a shift (iltifāt) from address to the third person. The discussion of iltifāt has preceded many times.
4- In His saying «فضرب بينهم بسور له باب باطنه فيه الرحمة وظاهره من قبله العذاب» there are two lofty devices. The first is the representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): He likened the hypocrites' remaining in the pitch-darkness of their hypocrisy and its gloom to one between whom and the guiding light a wall has been set up that screens off every light. The second device is antithesis (al-muqābala): He matched its inside with its outside, and mercy with punishment.

dervis-irab:16-20.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَأْنِ): the imperfect of «أنى يأني», of the pattern «رمى» [i.e. «رمى يرمي»]; it is weak (muʿtall), and the yāʾ that is its final radical was dropped because of the jussive particle, as will come in the I'rab. «أنى» means: its ināʾ, i.e. its time, has come. Ibn al-Sikkīt recited:
ألما يأن لي أن تجلّى عمايتي ... وأقصر عن ليلى بلى قد أنى لنا
(Has the time not yet come for my blindness to clear and for me to desist from Laylā? Yes, the time has come for us.)

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ وَما نَزَلَ مِنَ الْحَقِّ): the hamza is for interrogation; «لم» is a particle of negation, inversion (qalb) and jussive; «يأن» is an imperfect verb made jussive (majzūm) by «لم», the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter. «للذين» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element, its implied form being "I mean", so it is for clarification (tabyīn); this is what Abū al-Baqāʾ chose, but there is no need for it, so the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to «يأن». The clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun and has no grammatical position. «أن» with what falls within its scope is the fāʿil (agent) of «يأن», i.e. has the time of their hearts' humbling not drawn near, and has its time not come? Among this is the poet's saying:
ألم يأن لي يا قلب أن أترك الجهلا ... وأن يحدث الشيب المنير لنا عقلا
(Has the time not come, O heart, for me to leave folly, and for shining grey hair to produce in us some sense?)
«لذكر الله» is attached to «تخشع». The wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is a relative noun conjoined to «ذكر الله»; the clause «نزل» is the ṣila; «من الحق» is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَلا يَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتابَ مِنْ قَبْلُ فَطالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْأَمَدُ): the wāw is a conjunction; «لا» is negating; «يكونوا» is conjoined to «تخشع». It is also permissible that «لا» be prohibitive, in which case this is a transition to forbidding the believers from being like those who preceded them. «يكونوا» is a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb; the wāw is its noun and «كالذين» its khabar (predicate); the clause «أوتوا» is the ṣila; «الكتاب» is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «من قبل» is attached to «أوتوا»; «فطال» is conjoined to «أوتوا»; «عليهم» is attached to «طال»; «الأمد» is the fāʿil.
(فَقَسَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ): «فقست قلوبهم» is conjoined to «فطال عليهم الأمد». «كثير» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «منهم» is an adjective of «كثير», and for that reason it is allowable to begin with it; «فاسقون» is the khabar of «كثير».
(اعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يُحْيِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها): resumptive speech, set forth to address the believers mentioned, by way of shift (iltifāt). «اعلموا» is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; «أنّ» with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of «اعلموا». «أنّ» and its noun, and the clause «يحيي الأرض» is the khabar of «أنّ»; the adverb is attached to «يحيي»; «موتها» is muḍāf ilayhi.
(قَدْ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ الْآياتِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ): «قد» is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); «بيّنّا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «لكم» is attached to «بيّنّا»; «الآيات» is the object; «لعلّ» and its noun, and the clause «تعقلون» is its khabar.
(إِنَّ الْمُصَّدِّقِينَ وَالْمُصَّدِّقاتِ وَأَقْرَضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضاً حَسَناً يُضاعَفُ لَهُمْ وَلَهُمْ أَجْرٌ كَرِيمٌ): «إنّ» and its noun; «المصدقات» is conjoined to «المصدقين»; «أقرضوا» is conjoined to the meaning of the verb in «المصدقين», because the lām [i.e. the article «ال»] is in the sense of «الذين» and the active participle is in the sense of «اصّدّقوا», as though it were said "those who gave in charity and lent". The Word of Majesty (Allah) is the mafʿūl bihi; «قرضا» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) and «حسنا» a naʿt (adjective). «يضاعف» is a passive imperfect verb and «لهم» stands in place of the fāʿil; it is also permissible that what stands in place of the fāʿil be an implied pronoun referring to the [notion of] giving charity, and a muḍāf must then be omitted, i.e. the reward of giving charity; «لهم» is then attached to «يضاعف». The wāw is a conjunction; «لهم» is a fronted khabar and «أجر» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «كريم» is an adjective. [Translator's note: the khabar of «إنّ» is not explicitly named in the source.]
(وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ أُولئِكَ هُمُ الصِّدِّيقُونَ): the wāw is resumptive; «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ; the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila; «بالله» is attached to «آمنوا»; «رسله» is conjoined to «الله»; «أولئك» is a second mubtadaʾ. «هم» may be a pronoun of separation (faṣl), with «الصدّيقون» the khabar of «أولئك», and «أولئك» with its khabar the khabar of the first. It is also permissible that «هم» be a third mubtadaʾ and «الصدّيقون» its khabar, it with its khabar being the khabar of the second, and the second with its khabar the khabar of the first.
(وَالشُّهَداءُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ وَنُورُهُمْ): «الشهداء» may be conjoined to what precedes it, so the pause at it is complete; He informed about those who believed that they are truthful ones and witnesses. It is also permissible that the wāw be resumptive and «الشهداء» a mubtadaʾ, and you have two views on its khabar: one is that it is the adverb after it, and the second is that it is His saying «لهم أجرهم». «لهم» is a fronted khabar and «أجرهم» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «نورهم» is conjoined to «أجرهم»; the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl.
(وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا أُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ الْجَحِيمِ): «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ; the clause «كفروا» is the ṣila; «كذبوا» is conjoined to «كفروا»; «بآياتنا» is attached to «كفروا» [Translator's note: so in the source; the nearer verb is «كذبوا»]; «أولئك» is a mubtadaʾ and «أصحاب الجحيم» its khabar.
(اعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ وَزِينَةٌ وَتَفاخُرٌ بَيْنَكُمْ وَتَكاثُرٌ فِي الْأَمْوالِ وَالْأَوْلادِ): resumptive speech, set forth to belittle this world and the insignificance of its affair. «اعلموا» is an imperative verb indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; «أنّ» with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of «اعلموا»; «أنما» here is a restraining and restrained particle (kāffa wa-makfūfa) [i.e. «ما» stops «أنّ» from governing]. «الحياة» is a mubtadaʾ and «الدنيا» an adjective of it; «لعب» is the khabar of «الحياة», and what follows is coordinated with it; «بينكم» is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of «تفاخر»; «في الأموال» is an adjective of «تكاثر».
(كَمَثَلِ غَيْثٍ أَعْجَبَ الْكُفَّارَ نَباتُهُ ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَراهُ مُصْفَرًّا ثُمَّ يَكُونُ حُطاماً): the kāf is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the meaning of what preceded, i.e. these attributes are established for it, likened to rain. The clause «أعجب» is an adjective of «غيث»; «الكفار» is the fronted object of «أعجب», and they are the sowers; «نباته» is the postponed fāʿil. «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence with delay; «يهيج» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and its fāʿil is "هو", referring to the plants, i.e. it dries up; the triliteral «هاج» means "dried up". «فتراه» is conjoined to «يهيج»; the fāʿil of «تراه» is "أنت" and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; «مصفرّا» is a ḥāl because the seeing is visual. «ثم يكون حطاما» is conjoined to what preceded.
(وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِضْوانٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; «في الآخرة» is a fronted khabar and «عذاب» a postponed mubtadaʾ; «شديد» is an adjective of «عذاب»; «مغفرة» is conjoined to «عذاب»; «من الله» is an adjective of «مغفرة»; «رضوان» is conjoined to «مغفرة». More of the secrets of this construction will come in the Rhetoric section.
(وَمَا الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا إِلَّا مَتاعُ الْغُرُورِ): the wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is negating; «الحياة» is a mubtadaʾ and «الدنيا» an adjective of «الحياة»; «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); «الغرور» is muḍāf ilayhi, and the annexation is explicative (bayāniyya) [Translator's note: the source does not explicitly name «متاع» as the khabar]. Ghurūr, with ḍamma, is what a person is deceived by of the enjoyment of this world.

* Rhetoric:
1- The representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in His saying «اعلموا أن الله يحيي الأرض بعد موتها» there is a representative metaphor: He likened the softening of hearts by remembrance and recitation, after their hardness and their aversion to hearing the truth and acting on its commands, to the reviving of dead land by rain, in that each of them involves a thing reaching its expected perfection after being devoid of it. Or it is a representative metaphor for the reviving of the dead, in that He likened their reviving to the reviving of dead land, and that whoever is able to do the second is able to do the first; so it is fitting that hearts humble themselves at His remembrance.
2- In His saying «كمثل غيث أعجب الكفار نباته» (the verse) there is also a representative metaphor: it is a likeness of the life of this world, in the speed of its passing and the smallness of its benefit, to the state of plants that rain has caused to grow, so that they stood up straight and the tillers — or the unbelievers, according to a difference among the exegetes — admired them, because both these and those are the most intense in admiring the adornment of the life of this world.
3- Antithesis (al-ṭibāq): He set in antithesis, in His saying «وفي الآخرة عذاب», the punishment and the forgiveness in His saying «ومغفرة من الله ورضوان»; but it is an antithesis between one thing and two things, so it is of the type "one hardship will not overcome two eases". Its detail will come in Sūrat al-Inshirāḥ.

dervis-irab:21-25.t:
* I'rab:
(سابِقُوا إِلى مَغْفِرَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ): resumptive speech, set forth to explain the causes and means of true boasting, in which it is valid to take pride. «سابقوا» is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); «إلى مغفرة» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سابقوا»; «من ربكم» is a naʿt (adjective) of «مغفرة».
(وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُها كَعَرْضِ السَّماءِ وَالْأَرْضِ أُعِدَّتْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ): «جنة» is conjoined to «مغفرة»; «عرضها» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «كعرض السموات» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse here reads «السماء»] is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is an adjective of «جنة»; «الأرض» is conjoined to «السموات». «أعدّت» is a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "هي"; the clause is a second adjective of «جنة», and it may also be resumptive. «للذين» is attached to «أعدّت»; the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun and has no grammatical position; «بالله» is attached to «آمنوا»; «رسله» is conjoined to «بالله».
(ذلِكَ فَضْلُ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ): «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ and «فضل الله» the khabar; the clause «يؤتيه» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). «يؤتيه» is an imperfect verb, a latent fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); «من» is a relative noun in the position of accusative as the second object; the clause «يشاء» is the ṣila of «من». «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and «ذو الفضل العظيم» the khabar.
(ما أَصابَ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ إِلَّا فِي كِتابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ نَبْرَأَها): «ما» is negating; «أصاب» is a past verb. «من مصيبة»: «من» is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and «مصيبة» is genitive in form and nominative in position as the fāʿil of «أصاب»; the verb is masculine because the femininity of «مصيبة» is figurative. «في الأرض» is an adjective of «مصيبة», or attached to «أصاب», or to «مصيبة» itself. «ولا في أنفسكم» is conjoined to «في الأرض». «إلا» is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). «في كتاب» is a ḥāl of «مصيبة», since it is specified by the adjective, or by governing [something] if «في الأرض» is attached to it; or [it is attached] to an omitted element, its implied form being "except that it is existing in a book", so it is in the position of nominative as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. «من قبل» is attached to what His saying «في كتاب» is attached to, i.e. except established in a book before We create it. «نبرأها» is an imperfect verb made accusative by «أن»; the fāʿil is latent, referring to Allah the Exalted; the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, referring to the calamity — it was also said to the souls, and it was said to the earth. «أن» with what falls within its scope is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it, and the clause is in the position of genitive as an adjective of «كتاب». The pronoun in «نبرأها» refers to the calamity, or to the souls, or to the earth, or to all of that; and the meaning of «نبرأها» is "We create it".
(إِنَّ ذلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ): «إنّ» and its noun; «على الله» is attached to «يسير»; «يسير» is the khabar of «إنّ».
(لِكَيْلا تَأْسَوْا عَلى ما فاتَكُمْ وَلا تَفْرَحُوا بِما آتاكُمْ): the lām is a preposition, and «كي» is a maṣdar-forming particle equivalent to «أن»; it is not for causation, because if it were so another particle of causation would not enter upon it. «لا» is negating; «تأسوا» is an imperfect verb made accusative by «كي», the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. Its original form is «تأسيون»: the yāʾ was vowelled and what preceded it had fatḥa, so it was changed to alif, becoming «تأساون»; then two quiescent letters met, the alif and the wāw which is the fāʿil, so the alif was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "«أسي أسى», of the pattern «تعب», means he grieved, so he is «أسيّ» on the pattern faʿīl, like «حزين»." The genitive-governing lām with what falls within its scope is attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "and We informed you" or "We told you"; some implied it as "We tested you". The wāw is a conjunction; «لا» is negating; «تفرحوا» is conjoined to «تحزنوا» [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb in the verse is «تأسوا»]; «بما» is attached to «تفرحوا»; the clause «آتاكم» is the ṣila. The complement of «فاتكم» and «آتاكم» is omitted, its implied form being "of blessings".
(وَاللَّهُ لا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ مُخْتالٍ فَخُورٍ): «الله» is a mubtadaʾ and the clause «لا يحبّ» the khabar; «كل مختال» is the mafʿūl bihi and «فخور» an adjective.
(الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ وَيَأْمُرُونَ النَّاسَ بِالْبُخْلِ): «الذين» is a badal (substitute) for His saying «كل مختال فخور», as though He said: He does not love those who are stingy. It may also be in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ with its khabar omitted, the implied form being "for they deserve punishment"; it is also valid for it to be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "they are those who", or accusative for blame by an omitted verb, its implied form being "I blame". These views are all equal in preference. The clause «يبخلون» is the ṣila of the relative noun and has no grammatical position; «يأمرون» is conjoined to «يبخلون»; «الناس» is the mafʿūl bihi; «بالبخل» is attached to «يأمرون». Some considered the badal and the adjective readings far-fetched and made it a complete resumptive [speech] with no connection to what precedes it.
(وَمَنْ يَتَوَلَّ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَمِيدُ): the wāw is resumptive; «من» is a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, a mubtadaʾ; «يتولّ» is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) because it occurs as a nominal clause; «إنّ» and its noun; «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) — in one reading it is dropped, which supports its being a [pronoun of] separation [Translator's note: the source says «فعلا» ("a verb"), evidently a slip for «فصلا» ("separation")] and not a mubtadaʾ; «الغني» is the khabar of «إنّ» and «الحميد» a second khabar; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis.
(لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا رُسُلَنا بِالْبَيِّناتِ): the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; «قد» is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); «أرسلنا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «رسلنا» is the mafʿūl bihi; «بالبيّنات» is a ḥāl; the clause is resumptive.
(وَأَنْزَلْنا مَعَهُمُ الْكِتابَ وَالْمِيزانَ لِيَقُومَ النَّاسُ بِالْقِسْطِ): «أنزلنا» is conjoined to «أرسلنا»; «معهم» is an adverb of place attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. and We sent down the Book in a state of its coming to be and becoming with them when it reached them on earth. «الكتاب» is the mafʿūl bihi and «الميزان» is conjoined to «الكتاب». The lām is for causation; «يقوم» is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied «أن» after the lām; «بالقسط», i.e. with justice, is attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. acting equitably and justly; you may also attach it to «يقوم». The lām and its genitive noun are attached to «أرسلنا» and «أنزلنا», because it is the cause of the sending and the sending down.
(وَأَنْزَلْنَا الْحَدِيدَ فِيهِ بَأْسٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَنافِعُ لِلنَّاسِ): the wāw is a conjunction; «أنزلنا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «الحديد» is the mafʿūl bihi; «فيه» is a fronted khabar and «بأس» a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is a ḥāl of «الحديد»; «شديد» is an adjective, i.e. in it is strength and protection — the discussion of this is long; «منافع للناس» is conjoined to «بأس شديد». Hardly any craft is free of iron.
(وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَنْصُرُهُ وَرُسُلَهُ بِالْغَيْبِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ): the wāw is a conjunction; «ليعلم» is conjoined to an omitted element indicated by the clause «فيه بأس شديد», so it is a cause for the causation [stated there], not a cause for the sending and the sending down. By this you know the error of the saying of some grammarians, such as al-Jalāl and others, that it is conjoined to «ليقوم». «الله» is the fāʿil and «من» the mafʿūl bihi; the clause «ينصره» is the ṣila of «من»; «رسله» is conjoined to the hāʾ, i.e. and helps His messengers as well; «بالغيب» is a ḥāl of the hāʾ of «ينصره», i.e. He being absent from them in this world. [Then] «إنّ» and its noun and its two predicates.

* Benefits:
Conjoining to the overt noun and to the pronoun: one conjoins to the overt noun and to the detached pronoun, whether nominative or accusative, and to the attached accusative pronoun, without condition, as in "قام زيد وعمرو" (Zayd and ʿAmr stood), "أنا وأنت قائمان" (I and you are standing) and "إياك والأسد" (beware of the lion). Conjoining to the attached accusative pronoun is as in «جمعناكم والأولين»: «الأولين» is conjoined to the kāf. It is not good to conjoin to the attached nominative pronoun, whether overt or latent, except after emphasising it with a detached pronoun, as in «لقد كنتم أنتم وآباؤكم» and «اسكن أنت وزوجك الجنة». Ibn Mālik pointed to this in al-Khulāṣa [the Alfiyya] with his saying:
وإن على ضمير رفع متصل ... عطفت فافصل بالضمير المنفصل
(If you conjoin to an attached nominative pronoun, separate with the detached pronoun.)

dervis-irab:26-29.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَقَفَّيْنا): taqfiya is placing a thing in the track of a thing, continuing in it. For this reason the endings of verse are called qawāfī (rhymes), since they follow the line in its track, continuing in another [line] according to its pattern. In al-Mukhtār: "«قفا أثره» means he followed it, and its pattern is «عدا» [i.e. «عدا يعدو»]; «قفّى على أثره بفلان» means he made So-and-so follow him; from it is the saying of Allah the Exalted «ثم قفينا على آثارهم برسلنا», and from it is rhymed speech (al-kalām al-muqaffā)."
(وَرَهْبانِيَّةً): rahbāniyya (monasticism) is excess in worship and spiritual discipline and cutting oneself off from people, attributed to the rahbān, who is the one excessive in fear, from «رهب», like khashyān from «خشي». It was also read with ḍamma [«رُهبانية»], as though attributed to ruhbān, the plural of rāhib, like rākib and rukbān. The wording of al-Qāmūs: "The rāhib is the singular of the ruhbān (monks) of the Christians; its maṣdar is rahba and rahbāniyya. Or ruhbān, with ḍamma, may be a singular, and its plural is rahābīn, rahābina and ruhbānūn. There is no monasticism in Islam: it is like castration, wearing chains, wearing sackcloth, abandoning meat and the like." The author of al-Munjid was content with saying: "Ruhbāniyya and rahbāniyya: the way of the monks", and he defined the rāhib by saying: "One who withdraws from people to a monastery seeking worship." More of its meaning will come in the I'rab section.
(كِفْلَيْنِ): two large portions. Kifl is a share; from it is the kifl that the rider takes as a safeguard, which is a cloak or the like that he wraps around [the saddle] on camels when he wants to sleep, so that it keeps him from falling; so there is in it a share of protection from falling.

* I'rab:
(وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً وَإِبْراهِيمَ وَجَعَلْنا فِي ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا النُّبُوَّةَ وَالْكِتابَ): the wāw is a conjunction; the lām is the answer to the omitted oath; «قد» is a particle of realization (taḥqīq); the oath is repeated to show greater concern for the matter. «أرسلنا» is a verb and its fāʿil (agent); «نوحا» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and «إبراهيم» is conjoined to «نوحا». «جعلنا» is conjoined to «أرسلنا»; «في ذريتهما» is in the position of the second object; «النبوة» is the first object of «جعلنا»; «الكتاب» is conjoined to «النبوة». By «الكتاب» He meant the genus, i.e. the four books.
(فَمِنْهُمْ مُهْتَدٍ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ): the fāʾ is for consequence (tafrīʿ); «منهم» is a fronted khabar (predicate) and «مهتد» a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); «كثير» is a mubtadaʾ, «منهم» a naʿt (adjective) of «كثير», and «فاسقون» the khabar of «كثير».
(ثُمَّ قَفَّيْنا عَلى آثارِهِمْ بِرُسُلِنا): «ثم» is a conjunction for sequence with delay; «قفينا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «على آثارهم» — the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قفينا»; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾid) preposition, and «رسلنا» is genitive in form and accusative in position.
(وَقَفَّيْنا بِعِيسَى ابْنِ مَرْيَمَ وَآتَيْناهُ الْإِنْجِيلَ): «قفينا» is conjoined to the first «قفينا». «بعيسى»: the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and «عيسى» is genitive in form and a mafʿūl bihi in position; «ابن» is a badal (substitute) and «مريم» is muḍāf ilayhi. «وآتيناه»: the wāw is a conjunction, and «آتيناه» is a verb, its fāʿil and the first mafʿūl bihi; «الإنجيل» is the second mafʿūl bihi.
(وَجَعَلْنا فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ رَأْفَةً وَرَحْمَةً وَرَهْبانِيَّةً ابْتَدَعُوها ما كَتَبْناها عَلَيْهِمْ إِلَّا ابْتِغاءَ رِضْوانِ اللَّهِ): «جعلنا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «في قلوب» is in the position of the second object; «الذين» is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause «اتبعوه», consisting of the verb, the fāʿil and the mafʿūl bihi, is the ṣila (relative clause). «رأفة» is the first mafʿūl bihi and «رحمة» the second mafʿūl bihi [Translator's note: so in the source; «رحمة» is evidently conjoined to «رأفة», as the next paragraph itself treats it]. On «رهبانية» there are two views:
1- The first is that it is coordinated with «رأفة» and «رحمة», and the clause «ابتدعوها» is an adjective of it. It was singled out by mention of innovating only because mercy and compassion in the heart are an innate matter in which man has no acquisition, unlike monasticism, for it is among the acts of the body and man has acquisition in it.
2- The second is that it is accusative by an implied verb that the overt one explains, so the question belongs to the chapter of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb with a pronoun). Al-Zamakhsharī, Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī and the Muʿtazila inclined to this i'rab. That is because they say: whatever is from man's act is created by him; so since compassion and mercy are from Allah's act, their creation or their being made was attributed to Him, and since monasticism is not from the act of Allah the Exalted but from the act of the servant, its creation was attributed to him.
Here, for the reader, is the text of Abū Ḥayyān's wording: "«ورهبانية» is conjoined to what precedes it, so it enters into the clauses, and the clause «ابتدعوها» is a clause in the position of an adjective of «رهبانية». Monasticism was singled out by innovating because in compassion and mercy in the heart man has no acquisition, unlike monasticism, for it is acts of the body together with something in the heart, so there is room in it for acquisition. Qatāda said: mercy is from Allah, and monasticism — they innovated it." Monasticism is rejecting this world and its desires, of women and others, and taking hermitages. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī made «ورهبانية» cut off from conjunction with what precedes it of «رأفة» and «رحمة», so for him «ورهبانية» is accusative by the implication of a verb explained by what follows it; so it is of the chapter of ishtighāl, i.e. "and they innovated monasticism — they innovated it". Al-Zamakhsharī followed him and said: "Its accusative is by an implied verb that the overt one explains, its implied form being 'and they innovated monasticism, they innovated it', meaning they originated it from themselves and vowed it." This is the i'rab of the Muʿtazila — Abū ʿAlī was a Muʿtazilī — and they say that what is created by Allah is not created by the servant; compassion and mercy are of Allah's creation, while monasticism is of man's innovation, so it is created by him. This i'rab of theirs is not good from the standpoint of the craft of Arabic, because something like this is of the kind in which the nominative as mubtadaʾ is not permissible, and beginning here with His saying «ورهبانية» is not permissible, because it is indefinite with none of the justifications for beginning with an indefinite noun.
Ibn al-Munayyir said, following up on al-Zamakhsharī: "In the i'rab of this verse Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī became entangled and sided with the faction of discord and the party of innovation: he parsed «رهبانية» as accusative by an implied verb that the overt one explains, and he gave a reason for the impossibility of conjunction, saying: 'Do you not see that monasticism cannot properly be construed with «جعلنا» while it is described by His saying «ابتدعوها», because what He, the Exalted, makes they do not innovate?' Al-Zamakhsharī too went down his blameworthy path, and his accursed devil handed him over: when he allowed what Abū ʿAlī had forbidden, namely making it conjoined, he excused that by distorting «الجعل» (making) to the meaning of granting success (tawfīq), fleeing from what Abū ʿAlī fled from — the belief that this is created by Allah the Exalted — and inclining to associating partners [with Allah] and the belief that what they themselves do Allah the Exalted does not lead astray [Translator's note: «لا يضلّه» as in the source; perhaps «لا يُحِلّه» or a similar word is meant] nor create. What is in this verse suffices as proof, after the decisive proofs and rational demonstrations, of the falsity of what the two of them believed: for the mention of the place of mercy and compassion, while it is known that their place is the accusative [Translator's note: «محلها النصب» as in the source; the sense seems to be that their place is known to be the heart], made His saying «في قلوب الذين اتبعوه» an emphasis of His creating these meanings and a depiction of the meaning of creation by mentioning its place. If what was meant were something not created in their hearts by Allah the Exalted, as the two of them claimed, His saying «في قلوب الذين اتبعوه» would have no place left, and Allah refuses that His noble Book should contain what has no place."
As for Abū al-Baqāʾ, he combined the two opinions and said: "The saying of Allah the Exalted «ورهبانية» is accusative by a verb indicated by «ابتدعوها», not by conjunction with «الرحمة», because what Allah the Exalted made they do not innovate. It was also said that it is conjoined to it, and «ابتدعوها» is an adjective of it; the meaning is: He imposed on them adherence to a monasticism that they innovated; for this reason He said «ما كتبناها عليهم إلا ابتغاء رضوان الله»."
As for Ibn Hishām, he said in al-Mughnī: "And al-Fārisī's saying about «ورهبانية ابتدعوها» that it is of the chapter of «زيدا ضربته»; Ibn al-Shajarī objected to him that the condition of the accusative noun in this chapter is that it be specified, so that its being nominative as mubtadaʾ is valid. The well-known view is that it is conjoined to what precedes it and «ابتدعوها» is an adjective, and a muḍāf must be implied, i.e. 'the love of monasticism' [Translator's note: the source has «وجد» (found), probably for «حبّ» (love) as in al-Mughnī]. Abū ʿAlī did not construe the verse in that way only because of his Muʿtazilism, so he said: because what they innovate Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not create."
The summary of the dispute is that if «ورهبانية» were made conjoined to what precedes it, there would be a contradiction in the speech: the import of the speech requires that monasticism be created by Allah, while the description of it by innovation requires that it be created by them, and what is created by them Allah does not create [on their view], so it is a contradiction. Therefore al-Fārisī, followed by al-Zamakhsharī, turned away from conjunction and made it of the chapter of ishtighāl. We have cited these sayings only to show you the effect that i'rab has on directing belief; for this reason we did not see any room for ourselves to prefer [one view]; so reflect.
We return to complete the i'rab of the verse and say: the clause «ابتدعوها» is either an adjective of «رهبانية» or explicative, according to the two views. «ما» is negating; «كتبناها» is a verb, its fāʿil and the mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is an adjective of «رهبانية» in any case; it may also be resumptive. «إلا» is a particle of exception if we consider the exception disjoined (munqaṭiʿ), or a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) if we consider it joined (muttaṣil). On the first, «ابتغاء» is parsed as a disjoined excepted noun, «إلا» being in the sense of «لكن», and the meaning is: We did not impose it on them, but they innovated it. On the second, «ابتغاء» is parsed as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and the meaning is: We did not prescribe it for them for any reason whatsoever except for seeking the good pleasure of Allah, and «كتب» is then in the sense of "decreed". Al-Zamakhsharī was content with the first view.
(فَما رَعَوْها حَقَّ رِعايَتِها): the fāʾ is a conjunction; «ما» is negating; «رعوها» is a verb, its fāʿil and the mafʿūl bihi; «حق رعايتها» is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
(فَآتَيْنَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْهُمْ أَجْرَهُمْ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنْهُمْ فاسِقُونَ): the fāʾ is a conjunction; «آتينا» is a verb and its fāʿil; «الذين» is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila of the relative noun; «منهم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «أجرهم» is the second mafʿūl bihi; «كثير» is a mubtadaʾ, «منهم» an adjective and «فاسقون» the khabar.
(يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَآمِنُوا بِرَسُولِهِ يُؤْتِكُمْ كِفْلَيْنِ مِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ): «يا» is a vocative particle; «أي» is the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; the hāʾ is for drawing attention; «الذين» is a badal; the clause «آمنوا» is the ṣila. «اتقوا الله» is an imperative verb, its fāʿil and the mafʿūl bihi; «آمنوا» is an imperative verb conjoined to «اتقوا»; «برسوله» is attached to «آمنوا». «يؤتكم» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the command, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the weak letter; the kāf is the first mafʿūl bihi and «كفلين» the second mafʿūl bihi; «من رحمته» is an adjective of «كفلين».
(وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ نُوراً تَمْشُونَ بِهِ): conjoined to «يؤتكم»; «لكم» is attached to «يجعل» or is in the position of the second object; «نورا» is the object of «يجعل»; the clause «تمشون به» is an adjective of «نورا».
(وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ): conjoined to what preceded; «لكم» is attached to «يغفر»; «الله» is a mubtadaʾ, «غفور» a first khabar and «رحيم» a second khabar.
(لِئَلَّا يَعْلَمَ أَهْلُ الْكِتابِ أَلَّا يَقْدِرُونَ عَلى شَيْءٍ مِنْ فَضْلِ اللَّهِ): the lām is the lām of causation; «أن» is a maṣdar-forming particle that makes the verb accusative; «لا» is redundant; «يعلم» is an imperfect verb made accusative by «أن», i.e. so that [they] may know your deeds by that [Translator's note: «أي ليعلم أعمالكم بذلك» as in the source]; so the lām is attached to an omitted element drawn from the meaning of the request clause. «أهل الكتاب» is the fāʿil of «يعلم». «أن» is lightened from the heavy [«أنّ»], and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); «لا» is negating; the clause «يقدرون» is the khabar of «أن», and the meaning is "that they are not able". «على شيء» is attached to «يقدرون»; «من فضل الله» is an adjective of «شيء»; «أن» with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of «يعلم».
(وَأَنَّ الْفَضْلَ بِيَدِ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ): the wāw is a conjunction; «أنّ» with what falls within its scope is conjoined to «أن لا يقدرون», falling within the scope of what is known. «أنّ» and its noun; «بيد الله» is the khabar of «أنّ»; the clause «يؤتيه» is resumptive or a second khabar of «أنّ»; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi and «من» the second mafʿūl bihi; the clause «يشاء» is the ṣila.
(وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ): «الله» is a mubtadaʾ, «ذو الفضل» its khabar and «العظيم» an adjective of «الفضل».

* Benefits:
A negation may intervene in the speech, and then «أن» must be made overt after the lām of causation to which «لا» is attached. If «أن» were implied here it would not be permissible, because implying it would lead to the preposition directly adjoining the particle of negation, and that is not permissible.
